request:
Do not globally serialize independent GitHub System Actions

## Problem

GitHub System Actions currently execute under one Run-wide lock.

As a result, independent actions such as comments to unrelated Issues or Pull Requests are serialized even when the Graph schedules them in parallel.

The global lock is broader than any demonstrated shared-state requirement. It appears to protect against possible races by preventing all GitHub actions from overlapping.

This weakens the Graph principle that independent ready steps can execute concurrently.

## Expected outcome

Do not globally serialize unrelated GitHub System Actions.

Remove the Run-wide action lock where no shared mutable state requires it.

If a concrete operation such as repeated publication of the same managed PR requires synchronization, keep only the smallest synchronization needed for that specific shared state rather than locking every GitHub action.

Independent actions should be able to execute concurrently when the Graph schedules them concurrently.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Do not prevent concurrency preemptively because a race might exist somewhere.

Synchronization should correspond to an actual shared-state invariant, not serve as a blanket safety mechanism.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
